Text: U.S. high-yield credit spreads reached their highest level in five months as a surge in corporate debt issuance tests investor demand, according to Goldman Sachs credit strategist Amanda Lynam. September issuance totaled $38.51 billion, making it the busiest month of the year for junk bonds, helped by large deals including SoftBank's $10 billion offering. Lynam said the market is showing signs of the same “indigestion” seen in investment-grade credit earlier this summer. With a heavy issuance calendar and rising bond yields, the extra yield investors demand to hold corporate junk bonds over Treasuries widened 12 basis points to 294 basis points on Friday, the highest since April. Average CCC-rated spreads reached 968 basis points, their highest since November 2023. Goldman has tracked nearly $600 billion of AI-related debt issuance this year, with only about 40% coming from hyperscalers, highlighting the broader exposure across the sector. $GS

When SpaceX went public at a $1.77 trillion valuation, clients who sold shares realized significant gains, while Goldman collected hundreds of millions of dollars in related fees, according to people familiar with the matter. Goldman’s bankers received about $100 million as lead advisers on the SpaceX IPO, while the firm’s asset- and wealth-management business had previously provided clients with access to private SpaceX investment opportunities.
